issues.title: AI Fabric definition mandates non-blocking Clos, contradicted by Oversubscription Ratio
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
Actually found and reported by @ayourtch (Andrew Yourtchenko) in his review of the -03 draft set (Major finding [F01]):

The **AI Fabric** definition says: "Implemented as a non-blocking Clos (fat-tree) topology running RoCEv2 or UET." But the doc's own **Oversubscription Ratio** entry explicitly allows 2:1/4:1 oversubscription "for inference fabrics" — such a fabric would fail its own AI Fabric definition.

Fix: make topology descriptive rather than mandatory.

comments.author: cpignata
comments.body: Fixed in 28e47ed.

issues.title: Oversubscription Ratio and Bisection Bandwidth definitions mutually inconsistent
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
Actually found and reported by @ayourtch (Andrew Yourtchenko) in his review of the -03 draft set (Major finding [F02]):

Per the **Bisection Bandwidth** entry, a non-blocking fabric's bisection bandwidth equals half the total edge bandwidth, i.e. edge:bisection = 2:1. But the **Oversubscription Ratio** entry says a 1:1 ratio (of the same edge/bisection quantities) is non-blocking — a direct contradiction.

Fix: redefine Oversubscription Ratio using the conventional leaf downlink:uplink definition, and note explicitly that it is distinct from the edge-to-bisection-bandwidth ratio.

comments.author: cpignata
comments.body: Fixed in 28e47ed.

issues.title: Zero Packet Loss target for UET contradicts its designed-for-lossy operation
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
Actually found and reported by @ayourtch (Andrew Yourtchenko) in his review of the -03 draft set (Major finding [F03]):

**Zero Packet Loss** says "For RoCEv2 and UET transports, zero packet loss is the target operating condition." This contradicts UET's designed-for-lossy operation (RUD retransmission across sprayed paths, packet trimming deliberately truncating packets), and conflates wire-level with application-visible loss.

Fix: restrict the zero-loss criterion to lossless RoCEv2 and define UET's loss treatment (zero application-visible loss, depending on transport service) separately.

comments.author: cpignata
comments.body: Fixed in 28e47ed.

issues.title: RoCEv2 "requires lossless fabric operation for correctness" is wrong
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
Actually found and reported by @ayourtch (Andrew Yourtchenko) in his review of the -03 draft set (Major finding [F06]):

**RoCEv2** says it "requires lossless fabric operation (PFC or equivalent) for correctness." This is technically wrong: Reliable Connected (RC) mode recovers loss via PSN-based go-back-N retransmission; losslessness is a performance necessity, not a correctness requirement (cf. Resilient RoCE, IRN). The companion tests themselves run RoCEv2 under loss.

Fix: reword to reflect losslessness as a performance necessity rather than a correctness requirement.

comments.author: cpignata
comments.body: Fixed in 28e47ed.

issues.title: Entropy Value carriage misdescribed vs UEC 1.0 specification
issues.author: cpignata
issues.body:
Actually found and reported by @ayourtch (Andrew Yourtchenko) in his review of the -03 draft set (Major finding [F07]):

**Entropy Value** was described as "A per-packet field in the UET header ... providing explicit spray entropy independent of the IP 5-tuple." This is externally verified wrong against the published UEC 1.0 materials: the Entropy Value is carried in the UDP source port (or the equivalent position in IP-only mode), which IS part of the IP 5-tuple. Test equipment built from the old definition would vary the wrong bytes.

Verified directly against the UEC 1.0.2 specification PDF before fixing (direct quote: "When UDP encapsulation is used, the udp.src_port field is used as the entropy").

Fix: corrected to reflect the entropy value is carried in the UDP source port field (or PDS Entropy Header in IP-only mode), as part of the 5-tuple.

comments.author: cpignata
comments.body: Fixed in 28e47ed, verified against the UEC 1.0.2 specification PDF.

Do we want to make make BusBw calculation strongly dependson NVIDIA Collective Communications Library (NCCL)?

```suggestion | **BusBW** | The effective data throughput per accelerator during a collective operation, computed as:

BusBW = (data_size × algo_factor) / time

algo_factor is a fixed normalization constant derived from the ideal ring algorithm for each collective type, applied regardless of the algorithm actually selected by the collective library at runtime. This makes BusBW algorithm-invariant: the same hardware moving the same data volume in the same time yields the same BusBW whether the library selects ring, tree, or recursive doubling. The algo_factor calculation MUST conform to the formula specified here.

Collective algo_factor
AllReduce 2 × (n−1) / n
AllGather (n−1) / n
ReduceScatter (n−1) / n
AllToAll (n−1) / n

n = number of participating accelerators.

Worked example — AllReduce, n=8, data_size=1 GB, time=10 ms:
algo_factor = 2 × (8−1) / 8 = 1.75
BusBW = (1 GB × 1.75) / 10 ms = 175 GB/s

Reports MUST state: collective type, algo_factor value, collective library name and version, and n. The algorithm actually selected by the library SHOULD be reported as diagnostic information when known. Units: GB/s or Gbps; reports MUST state which. | ```

pulls.title: Editorial pass: address Andrew Yourtchenko's review + acronym/inclusive-language cleanup
pulls.author: cpignata
pulls.body:
## Summary

Addresses the minor and editorial issues identified by Andrew Yourtchenko in his review of the draft set (-03), plus a broader editorial pass covering acronym consistency, inclusive language, and idnits hygiene.

- Fixed internal contradictions in glossary definitions: Ring Algorithm step counts (2(N-1) applies only to AllReduce), algo_factor's "ideal ring algorithm" claim (untrue for AllToAll), Incast wrongly blamed on ring-AllReduce, TTFT/Prefill Phase disagreeing on where token 1 originates, Gradient Sync's "once per layer" self-contradiction, and Primary/Secondary KPI tier membership inconsistent across three tables
- Added missing citations for externally coined terms: ZeRO, PagedAttention, Orca/continuous batching, Expert Choice Routing, Speculative Decoding, DeepEP, DCQCN
- Clarified KVCXL is a term of art for this document set (not a real library) and cited real analogues (NVIDIA NIXL, Mooncake TransferEngine, LMCache); clarified GIN predates UEC and cited NVSHMEM/IBGDA
- Added 10 missing acronyms to the shared Acronyms table (BSP, CXL, FRR, GPU, LLM, PCIe, RC, SPMD, ToR, ZeRO) and the previously-undefined BMWG
- Fixed wording/naming nits: RT naming, ROD's per-PDC (not per-QP) state, Warmup Period's overstated "mandatory" claim, Binary Search's unstated initial range, T_dispatch's unscoped batch size, Fabric_Goodput's cross-references to undefined terms
- Standardized multiplication notation to × throughout (was a mix of ×, x, and \*) and switched <=/>= to ≤/≥
- Unbolded RFC 2119 keywords for consistency with the companion documents; added missing NOT RECOMMENDED to the keyword list
- Reviewed for NIST IR 8366 inclusive-language guidance (no issues found)
- Fixed an Acknowledgments wording mismatch with the companion drafts and added Andrew Yourtchenko's review credit

pulls.title: Fix five Major findings from Andrew Yourtchenko's review
pulls.author: cpignata
pulls.body:
## Summary

Fixes the five Major findings from Andrew Yourtchenko's review of the -03 draft set that weren't included in the earlier editorial PR (#41, already merged).

- AI Fabric definition mandated non-blocking Clos, contradicted by the doc's own Oversubscription Ratio entry allowing 2:1/4:1 for inference fabrics; made topology descriptive rather than mandatory. Closes #42
- Oversubscription Ratio and Bisection Bandwidth were mutually inconsistent; Oversubscription Ratio now uses the conventional leaf downlink:uplink definition and explicitly notes the distinction. Closes #43
- Zero Packet Loss listed UET's target as zero wire-level loss, contradicting UET's designed-for-lossy operation (RUD retransmission, packet trimming); restricted the zero-loss criterion to RoCEv2 and defined UET's loss treatment separately. Closes #44
- RoCEv2 "requires lossless fabric operation for correctness" was wrong; RC recovers loss via PSN-based retransmission, so losslessness is a performance necessity, not a correctness requirement. Closes #45
- Entropy Value was described as independent of the IP 5-tuple; verified against the UEC 1.0.2 specification (direct quote: "the udp.src_port field is used as the entropy") and corrected to reflect it is carried in the UDP source port field. Closes #46
